entities.summary:
Antoine Girard de Saint-Amant, sieur, was a French poet born in unknown year and died on 1661-12-29. He was a prominent figure in the literary circle of Western Europe during the Early Modern era. 

His poetry, often infused with themes of love, nature, and the human condition, was widely admired by his contemporaries. Saint-Amant's work was also notable for its use of classical models and its exploration of the complexities of the human experience. 

His legacy can be seen in the many poets who followed in his footsteps, including Charles Perrault and Jean-Baptiste Rousseau. 

"The stars are the sparks of the divine fire," Saint-Amant wrote in one of his most famous poems, highlighting the poet's deep sense of spirituality and connection to the natural world.
